title: Choose the visual world for the fashion (streetwear / drops) theme
question: The roll assigned The Wheatpaste Wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Hues on every card stand in for the merchant's ColorTheme preset — the theme owns no palette.

options.label: The Wheatpaste Wall
options.lineage: fly-posted street walls — gig and drop posters pasted over each other, day-glo paper, overprinted SOLD OUT stamps
options.thesis: The store is a wall of posters: every slider image and every product is a pasted sheet, so the goods are the wall and nothing is drawn around them.
materials: poster paper on a rendered wall
options.viewport: Masthead = the store's wordmark as one oversized pasted sheet, nav as a row of strips pasted under it, cart a day-glo stub. Below: the wall — the merchant's slider images as two or three large overlapping posters, and the newest/featured products pasted as smaller posters around them, each with a printed fact strip (name · price) at its foot and a stamp for SALE / SOLD OUT / X LEFT. Six to ten products are visible before the first scroll. The next product group is the next stretch of wall.
options.risk: Skew, overlap and texture must stay tightly bounded (≤3° rotation, fixed pitch) or it turns into kitsch; textures cost paint time on low-end phones and need a flat fallback.

raised.raise: The ground is a material, not a colour: the wall is a rendered surface and sections stack as sheets with bare wall between them.
Facts live in one ruled place: every poster carries the same printed strip (name · price · stock) at its foot, tabular numerals, never floating.
Live events are scarce: NEW, SOLD OUT and X LEFT are the only stamped overprints and the only things that animate; the whole wall works from the keyboard.

options.label: The Release Board
options.lineage: sneaker drop calendars and release apps — dated rows, AVAILABLE / SOLD OUT status, the newest at the top
options.thesis: Every product is a dated release on a board; the home page is this week's drop list and the newest items always lead.
options.viewport: A date-stamped board: the newest products as large rows with image, name, price and AVAILABLE / SOLD OUT status; featured as a second column of smaller rows.
options.risk: This is where most streetwear stores land — familiar by design; it wins on clarity, not memory, and the platform has no drop dates, so the board orders by newest only.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.lineage: a rail concourse departure board at rush hour
options.thesis: The catalogue as a departure board: products are rows ranked by time, columns never move, only the flaps.
options.viewport: A full-width board of product rows (image · name · price · status) in fixed columns, flaps cascading when the sort changes.
options.case: Fuses well with drops (rows by newest, status per row) and holds product clarity; loses identification — a travel object, not the shopper's own world — and is imagery-poor for apparel.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty once the cascade is over; a board without photos sells trains, not clothes.

options.label: Telop Caption Field
options.lineage: variety-show telop captions — outlined multicolour type sized to the emotion, the frame as a live comic
options.thesis: Merchant photos are the frame; prices, names and NEW / SALE land on them as outlined captions that scale with the news.
options.viewport: A full-bleed photo field with products as captioned frames; big outlined price captions, a small grey caption for the quiet facts.
options.case: Holds identification — hype captions are the streetwear feed's own voice — but loses clarity: free placement over photos fights the merchant's imagery and RTL mirroring of placed captions is fragile.
options.risk: One loud caption too many and the photos cannot be seen; the energy must be rationed.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: the metro screen — flat tiles, giant lowercase, headlines cropped off the edge, chrome deleted
options.thesis: Categories and products are flat tiles on black; the store name is a giant cropped word, and the merchant primary floods every live state.
options.viewport: A cropped giant store name, a panorama of square tiles (photo tiles for products, colour tiles for categories) that scroll-snaps sideways.
options.case: Wins clarity — tiles are doors, the grid is strict — but loses identification: a Windows Phone idiom, not a streetwear one, and giant lowercase does not carry Arabic.
options.risk: Recognised as an OS, not a shop; the light-weight lowercase voice is the opposite of poster caps.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: a surreal quarry where workers cut blocks of weather
options.thesis: Content as cut blocks with sky-blue voids between them.
options.viewport: Stacked white blocks with deep blue gaps.
options.risk: Nobody shopping for a hoodie identifies with meteorological masonry.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience identification and the blocks hide the goods.
options.kept: The ground is a material, not a colour — the wall is rendered and sections stack as sheets with bare wall between.

options.label: Blacksmith Scale Shower
options.lineage: a white-hot bar under a power hammer
options.thesis: One blow per full-width row, measured like a smith's chalk marks.
options.risk: A forge sells tools and drama, not tees.
options.case: Loses both axes: no identification for streetwear and the dark forge ground swallows merchant photos.
options.kept: Facts in one ruled place: every poster's printed strip (name · price · stock) sits at the same foot position with tabular numerals.

options.label: ANSI BBS Nightboard
options.lineage: a dial-up bulletin board at 2 a.m.
options.thesis: Everything is a text screen with numbered exits.
options.viewport: Centered title art over numbered menu lines.
options.risk: A text-only shop cannot show a jacket.
options.case: Loses both axes: a catalogue without images fails clarity and the audience is cook-group adjacent at best.
options.kept: Live events are scarce and precious: NEW / SOLD OUT / X LEFT are the only overprints that move, and the whole wall runs from the keyboard.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Black-and-white streetwear brutalism: giant caps wordmark, full-bleed lookbook hero, SHOP NOW, a four-column grid — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed model photo with the wordmark over it and one CTA, then the grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other streetwear store by design.
